test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 24 May 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If the numerator of a fraction be increased by 50% and its denominator be diminished by 28%, the value of the fraction is frac{{25}}{{36}} Find the original fraction.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Original Fraction = (Resulting Fraction) × (100 − %Decrease in Denom) / (100 + %Increase in Num)

Original Fraction = (25/36) × (72 / 150)

Simplify: (25/150) × (72/36) = (1/6) × 2

Original Fraction = 2/6 = 1/3

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in Numerator = 50%

Decrease in Denominator = 28%

Resulting Fraction = 25/36

 
 Original
 x / y
 
 
• 
 

 
 Num: +50%
 Den: −28%
 
 
 New Fraction
 25 / 36
 
 x × 150% / y × 72% = 25 / 36

**Calculation:**

Let the original fraction be x/y.

⇒ New Numerator = x + 50% of x = 1.5x

⇒ New Denominator = y − 28% of y = 0.72y

⇒ According to the question: 1.5x / 0.72y = 25/36

⇒ (x/y) × (150/72) = 25/36

⇒ x/y = (25/36) × (72/150)

⇒ x/y = (25/150) × (72/36)

⇒ x/y = (1/6) × 2

⇒ x/y = 2/6 = 1/3

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To increase a value by a%, multiply it by (100+a)/100. To decrease by b%, multiply by (100−b)/100.

Reciprocal Property

When moving a fraction from one side of an equation to another, it is multiplied by its reciprocal: (a/b) × x = c → x = c × (b/a).

Base 100 Method

Assuming the original parts as 100x and 100y simplifies the percentage calculation to 150x and 72y respectively.</p
